Q: Parent-child table with linked list under parent: can the CTE be reduced? A:

1. Data model changes

I'd simplify the model.

You just need the node's id and its parent to get the tree.

Then you just need one more column (I copied your prev) to order it.

2. Double recursive walk

First you walk the nodes that share a parent, to turn the prev values into idx values.

Then, a normal recursive walk, to give all nodes their level

3. Use floats to calculate relative positions

Imagine all nodes have a position value between 0.0 and 1.0

As the first level has 3 nodes, we need to space them 1/4 apart.

  • parent = position 0.00
  • child 1 = position 0.25
  • child 2 = position 0.50
  • child 3 = position 0.75

We can do the same, with smaller and smaller offsets as we go deeper into the tree.

To make it simpler, the answer below works out the largest number of nodes at the same vertex, once, and shrinks the position offsets by the same amount at every level.

In the example bekiw test is the position that should be inferred from the other columns. If the output has this column out of order, it fails the test.

CREATE TABLE map (
  id       INT,
  parent   INT,
  prev     INT,
  test     INT
);

INSERT INTO
  map
VALUES
( 0, null, null,  1),
(10,    0, null,  2),
( 1,   10, null,  3),
( 3,   10,    1,  4),
( 7,   10,    3,  5),
(14,    7, null,  6),
(12,    7,   14,  7),
(15,    0,   10,  8),
( 9,   15, null,  9),
( 8,   15,    9, 10), 
( 5,    0,   15, 11),
( 6,    5, null, 12),
( 2,    5,    6, 13),
( 4,    5,    2, 14),
(13,    4, null, 15),
(11,    4,   13, 16),
(22,    4,   11, 17)
;

WITH RECURSIVE
  ordered_under_parent(
    id,
    parent,
    idx,
    test
  )
AS
(
  SELECT
    id, parent, 1, test
  FROM
    map 
  WHERE
    prev IS NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
     c.id, c.parent, p.idx+1, c.test
  FROM
     ordered_under_parent   p
  INNER JOIN
     map                    c
       ON c.prev = p.id
),
  tree(
    id,
    parent,
    level,
    idx,
    test,
    pos,
    gap,
    factor
  )
AS
(
  SELECT
    id,
    parent,
    0,
    idx,
    test,
    0,
    1.0,
    (SELECT MAX(idx)+1 FROM ordered_under_parent)
  FROM
    ordered_under_parent
  WHERE
    parent IS NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
     c.id,
     c.parent,
     p.level+1,
     c.idx,
     c.test,
     p.pos
     +
     (c.idx * p.gap / p.factor),
     p.gap / p.factor,
     p.factor
  FROM
    tree                   p
  INNER JOIN
    ordered_under_parent   c
      ON c.parent = p.id
)
SELECT
  substr('..........',1,level*3) || id,
  *
FROM
  tree
ORDER BY
  pos
;

The following is probably a faster way to calculate factor, as it doesn't reference the recursive CTE.

(SELECT COUNT(*) + 1 FROM map GROUP BY parent ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1)

Q: Difference between 8086 and x86 assembly language A:
  • 8086 was the original CPU in the series
  • 8088 was an version of the CPU with a reduced bus width to save money, it was used in the original IBM PC and the PC/XT.
  • 80186 was a variant of the CPU designed to integrate more functionality and hence require less support circuitry than the original 8086/8088, but because it was designed before the PC took off it was not designed to be PC compatible. This limited its popularity.
  • 80286 was an improved variant with separate data and address busses and the first version of "protected mode". It was used in the IBM PC/AT.
  • 80386 added (among many other things) 32-bit mode.
  • 80486 added (among many other things) on-chip cache.

In practice people often left off the "80", refering to the chips as simply 286, 386, 486 and so-on. x86 came to be used to refer to the family as a whole.

After the 486, Intel decided to give their chips names instead of numbers, on the grounds that names could be trademarked and numbers could not. However, 586 and 686 neverthless came to be used to describe classes of CPUs in the sofware development world.

Confusingly AMD and Cyrix released processors under the 5x86 name. Despite the marketing these are largely fast 486-class processores. Similarly Cyrix released the 6x86 processor which while marketed against the Pentium Pro was really a fast Pentium-class processor.

Often suffixes are added to indicate the operating mode, e.g. x86-32 for 32-bit mode on the 386 and newer and x86-64 for the 64-bit mode on the Athlon64 and newer.

Nowadays if someone talks about x86 assembly language they might be talking about any version of the architecture, but are more likely talking about the 32-bit or 64-bit variants as those are what are still common today.

On the other hand if someone talks about 8086 assembly language they are likely talking about 16-bit real mode.

Q: Can you create feature branch from main and than merge it to develop branch? A:

Sounds like a usual hotfix, when "main promotion path" includes testing before deploying it's okay.

A hotfix shall not contain new features from develop but must be included in develop asap for the next release.

I would consider rebasing develop on top of the new main AFTER the feature was merged back into main. Then test and fix develop, which could cause a lot of work but thats the tradeof for an hotfix.

Q: Excel - paste special HTML option A:

This is a bit of code but seems to function OK. It uses Ron de Bruin's RangetoHTML function to create an HTML representation of the range to be copied, then adds a "magic" wrapper which signals to Excel that the HTML format is available, and adds the wrapped HTML to the clipboard.

If anyone knows where I got that "wrapper" code from please add a note in a comment. Background at this link: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dataxchg/html-clipboard-format#:~:text=The%20CF_HTML%20clipboard%20format%20allows,based%20on%20IE4/MSHTML%20implementations.

See the link for the RangetoHTML function.

Sub TestCopyRangeAsHtml()
    
    Dim html As String, ws As Worksheet
    
    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    
    html = RangetoHTML(ws.Range("B2:E6")) 'See https://jkp-ads.com/rdb/win/s1/outlook/bmail2.htm
    set_clipboard_text wrapHTML(html)     'put wrapped HTML in the clipboard
    
    ws.Range("G2").Select    'must select before pasting
    ActiveSheet.PasteSpecial 'paste as HTML
End Sub

'Not sure where I got this from...
'The "wrapper" lets Excel know the format is HTML
Private Function wrapHTML(ByVal html As String) As String
    Dim sData As String
    Const sContextStart = "<HTML><BODY><!--StartFragment -->"
    Const sContextEnd = "<!--EndFragment --></BODY></HTML>"
    Const sHtmlHeader = _
            "Version:1.0" & vbCrLf & _
            "StartHTML:<{]aaaaaaa" & vbCrLf & _
            "EndHTML:<{]bbbbbbb" & vbCrLf & _
            "StartFragment:<{]ccccccc" & vbCrLf & _
            "EndFragment:<{]dddddddd" + vbCrLf
    sData = sHtmlHeader & sContextStart & html & sContextEnd
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]aaaaaaa", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]bbbbbbb", Format(Len(sData), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]ccccccc", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader & sContextStart), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]ddddddd", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader & sContextStart & html), "0000000000"))
    wrapHTML = sData
End Function

'https://stackoverflow.com/a/78329329/478884
Function set_clipboard_text(str_text)
    On Error GoTo err_handler
    Dim MSForms_DataObject As Object
    Set MSForms_DataObject = CreateObject("new:{1C3B4210-F441-11CE-B9EA-00AA006B1A69}")
    MSForms_DataObject.SetText str_text
    MSForms_DataObject.PutInClipboard
    Set MSForms_DataObject = Nothing
    set_clipboard_text = True
    Exit Function
err_handler:
    Debug.Print "error in set_clipboard_text function. Err: " & _
    Err.description
set_clipboard_text = False
End Function

Q: How do I further optimize this prefix sum question? A:

It's a lot more readable, but still be careful with #include <bits/stdc++.h> as unless you use it in conjunction with precompiled headers it can slow the build process dramatically along with its other unsavoury effects (like this trivial example where it combines with using namespace std; to break the build after a compiler update). And you owe it to yourself to take a closer look at the Standard library containers, specifically std::vector as a replacement for int *ExitTime and int *BribeSum; and the subsequent manual management of they arrays they point at. There is a small performance hit, std::vector default-initializes all of its contents when presized, that may show up in competitive programming. If that performance hit is significant enough to care about, consider using std::unique_ptr before using new and picking up responsibility for the clean-up. Another good habit to get into is to not define a variable before you can completely initialize it. Sucks to waste time debugging because the program found a way around the deferred initialization. Also avoid macro #define constants in favour of constexpr constants. #define is simple text substitution that occurs before the compiler can apply sensible rules, leading to utterly bizarre compiler errors.

Q: Removing directory contents while ignoring a pattern in Python A:

The simplest approach is to iterate over the directory contents and filter using fnmatch:

import os
import shutil
import fnmatch

def rmtree_ignore(path, *patterns):
    for item in os.listdir(path):
        # Skip files/folders matching the pattern
        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(item, pattern) for pattern in patterns):
            continue
        
        full_path = os.path.join(path, item)
        if os.path.isdir(full_path):
            shutil.rmtree(full_path)
        else:
            os.remove(full_path)

# Usage - same syntax as ignore_patterns
rmtree_ignore('/tmp/my_dir', '*.pyc', 'tmp*')

If you want to keep the same API as copytree with ignore_patterns, you can reuse shutil.ignore_patterns directly:

import os
import shutil

def rmtree_ignore(path, ignore=None):
    if ignore is None:
        shutil.rmtree(path)
        return
    
    items = os.listdir(path)
    ignored = ignore(path, items)  # ignore_patterns returns a set of ignored names
    
    for item in items:
        if item in ignored:
            continue
        full_path = os.path.join(path, item)
        if os.path.isdir(full_path):
            shutil.rmtree(full_path)
        else:
            os.remove(full_path)

# Usage
rmtree_ignore('/tmp/my_dir', ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('*.pyc', 'tmp*'))

The second approach is cleaner — shutil.ignore_patterns() returns a callable that takes (directory, contents) and returns a set of names to skip, so you can reuse it directly without reimplementing the pattern matching logic.
